hints: Look at the block face-on, in the plane of the wall. Which forces act in that plane, and in which direction would the block slide?
worded:
1. In the plane of the wall two forces act: the weight 6 N (down) and the 8 N horizontal push. Their resultant is 10 N, at an angle below the horizontal.

2. The wall’s normal force is 10 N (balancing the push into the wall), so friction can be at most 0.25 × 10 = 2.5 N.

3. 10 N exceeds 2.5 N, so the block slides along the resultant’s direction, and kinetic friction acts directly against it.

4. Net force 10 − 2.5 = 7.5 N, so a = 7.5/0.6 = 12.5 m/s². (C)
conventional:
![](asset:P000538-sol-1)

In the plane of the wall: $F_{in - plane} = \sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}} = 10$ N. Normal force $N = 10$ N, so $f = \mu N = 2.5$ N, opposite to the motion.

$$a = \frac{10 - 2.5}{0.6} = 12.5\ {m/s}^{2}.$$
mistakes: Friction opposes the actual direction of sliding (along the 10 N resultant), not just the weight.

check.solved_answer: (C) 12.5 m/s², along the resultant of the weight and the 8 N force.
